#+TITLE: Vendored transport sources

* Native dependency

=nng-sys= is imported from the published =1.4.0-rc.0= crate, whose archive
SHA256 is =50d0e7f39a8fd1792a710da9351320e864dc799cf439960e332c977b2f876da6=.
Its bundled native library reports NNG 1.4.0. The MIT licenses remain in
=nng-sys/LICENSE= and =nng-sys/nng/LICENSE.txt=; upstream tests remain present.
Registry cache markers are not part of this source import. Two comments use
the standards names =RFC 6455= and =NIST 800= with space-separated numbering.

* Rust wrapper and dependency selection

=nng= is imported from the published =1.0.1= crate, whose archive SHA256 is
=20a18ed7ec1c8ff1658bcfea2ce76dcedf8be21dd9e8dd2e9762ba9632d16203=.
Its MIT license remains in =nng/LICENSE=. The root dependency selects this
wrapper by path, and the wrapper selects =../nng-sys= by path. Both
=bank-rpc= and =history-nng= therefore select the patched native source in
checkout builds, Git-source consumers, and native wheels built from them.
This does not depend on a workspace-root =[patch.crates-io]= override.

Cargo rewrites path dependencies to their registry versions when publishing
a crate. The version fields are compatibility constraints, not evidence that
a registry release contains this repair. A crates.io source distribution
requires its own dependency provenance check; the local path repair alone
does not establish that release's native implementation.

* Pair0 callback ordering

=pair0_pipe_stop= drains send and receive callbacks before clearing the
socket's peer and readiness under its mutex. Waiting occurs outside that
mutex because successful callbacks acquire it to publish readiness. Thus a
successful receive callback cannot leave =rd_ready=true= with a null peer.
Cancellation callbacks remain possible when an already-stopped operation is
reused; they do not publish readiness. This changes native lifecycle ordering,
not the Rust API, Pair0 wire format, or anneal's application framing.

The regression surface includes catalogue event replay, terminal delivery,
write-half closure, buffered full-duplex delivery and disconnect handoff.
